title: Sine-weighted Moving Average (SINEMA)
summary: A moving average whose weights follow half a sine wave across the window, so the middle bars count most and the line runs smooth.
descriptionHtml:
The Sine-weighted Moving Average spreads half a sine wave across its window. With p bars in the window, the bar k bars back weighs sin(pi * (k + 1) / p): small at the newest bar, largest near the middle, and zero at the oldest, so in effect the average covers the newest p - 1 bars. The weighted sum of the source is divided by the sum of the weights.

The window grows with the data until it reaches period, so the line starts on the first bar. A missing price is left out together with its weight, and a window whose weights add to zero shows the source itself.
howToReadHtml:
Read it as a smooth trend line. The rounded weights damp single-bar noise more than a simple average while keeping a similar lag of about half the window. A rising line with price above it describes an uptrend, and a falling line with price below it a downtrend; a change in the line's slope is the signal to watch.

Because the newest bar carries little weight, the line reacts to a sudden move a few bars later than a front-weighted average would. Until period bars exist the window is shorter.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many bars the half sine wave spans. A longer period gives a smoother, slower line.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series that is averaged, the close by default.

faq.q: Why does the newest bar weigh so little?
faq.html: The sine wave starts near zero at the newest bar and peaks in the middle of the window. That rounded shape is what makes the line smooth, at the cost of reacting a little later.

faq.q: How does it compare with a simple average?
faq.html: Over the same period it lags about as much but is smoother, because the edges of the window fade in and out instead of switching on and off.

faq.q: What does a period of 1 show?
faq.html: The source itself: a one-bar window averages just the current price. A period of 2 also follows the source, because the older of its two bars weighs zero.

related.title: Simple Moving Average (SMA)
related.summary: The plain average of the last N prices, with every bar in the window counted equally, drawn from the very first bar of the chart.

related.title: Savitzky-Golay Moving Average (SGMA)
related.summary: A symmetric weighted average over an odd window: a fixed coefficient table for degree 2 on 5, 7 or 9 bars, and a polynomial weight shape otherwise.

related.title: SP15: Spencer 15-Point Moving Average
related.summary: A fixed 15-bar weighted average of the close, with weights chosen so that cycles four and five bars long are removed rather than only damped.
